messages.subject: Help inserting regression lines
parts:
Hello, I'm new to geomorph and an archaeologist, to boot. I've been working with artifact shapes (projectile points) and am exploring the allometries for 3 significantly different groups. (Allometry works backwards in this case (i.e., the specimens get shorter as they are sharpened).) I've worked through the procD.allometry instructions and determined the allometries are significantly different. I'd like insert regression lines for each group to illustrate the differences in the plot, but I can't figure out how that's done.

I think I see a work around by creating a scatterplot of regression scores~logCsize and then following some instructions I found in the Scatterplot manual, but that seems inelegant.

Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

Dave

library(devtools) #improved geomorph is not yet approved by CRAN

library(geomorph)

setwd("D:/Documents/Analysis IV/MJ fewer LMs")

FFPEntire<-readland.tps("IV FFP 164 Entire 34 LMs.TPS", specID = "ID")

groups<-read.csv("R_FFP_Entire_Base_Classifiers.csv",header=TRUE,stringsAsFactors = TRUE) 
type<-as.factor(groups$TypeE5) 
Y.gpa<-gpagen(FFPEntire)

                                      logsz = TRUE, data=gdf, iter=10000, RRPP=TRUE, print.progress = FALSE)

plot(FFPEntireAllometry, method="RegScore")

     predictor = log(gdf$Csize), 
     reg.type = "RegScore",
     pch = 21,
     bg = as.numeric(gdf$Treatment),
     xlab = "log(CS)")

Thanks,
Dave

parts:
David, 


You did not follow the instructions in the help file. The example using procD.lm shows the original variables being added: 


## From help file: 

data(larvalMorph)
Y.gpa <- gpagen(larvalMorph$tailcoords, curves = larvalMorph$tail.sliders, print.progress = FALSE)
gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(Y.gpa, Treatment = larvalMorph$treatment, 
Family = larvalMorph$family)

# procD.lm approach, including interaction
tailAllometry2 <- procD.lm(coords ~ log(Csize) * Treatment, data = gdf, iter = 149, 
     print.progress = FALSE)
plot(tailAllometry2, type = "regression", 
predictor = log(gdf$Csize), 
reg.type = "PredLine",

pch = 21, 
bg = as.numeric(gdf$Treatment),

xlab = "log(CS)") # greater flexibility



If you follow precisely what shown in the help file that should get you closer to your goal.

Guillermo,

If you aspire to combine different values (say fitted values and residuals) in the same ordination, I recommend taking control of it from the start with an eigen-analysis of the covariance matrix you think is appropriate (could be fitted values or the general data covariance matrix), followed by projection of the different parts onto the eignevectors.  It seems you are trying to combine things that were obtained with different eigenvectors, which just does not make sense.

Remember that before projection, whatever you are projecting should be mean-centered.  For example, if you obtain a set of eignevectors, maybe from the eigen function in R, called E,

Pf <- scale(F, scale = FALSE) %*% E

projects the fitted values onto the eigenvectors and

Pr <- scale(R, scale = FALSE) %*% E

projects the residuals onto the same eigenvectors.  The two sets of principal component (projected) scores can then be combined into the same plot.

Cheers!
Mike
